title: Pages that connect — the screens, round 2

steps.path: Pages → Task board, the first time it opens
steps.headline: Step 1 is now only what the page may do, with a Continue button. No key symbol, no key box, no "everything else" line.
steps.changed: From your note: the permission and the key entry are separate things. The card holds the sentence alone; Continue leads to the key. A page that needs no new key still says Allow and open here.
steps.notice: The first card is shorter and reads the same for every kind of page.
steps.risk: One more press for pages that need a key.

steps.headline: Step 2 is the key: where to find it, the box, one plain line, then Allow and open.
steps.changed: New. The three instructions come with the page, written by whoever made it, and are labelled as the author's words. A page without instructions shows a general pointer: sign in on the service's website and look for API, Developer or Integrations. Under the box is one line only: "YouCoded keeps your key. The page never sees it."
steps.notice: A non-technical person is told where to click, not just asked for a key.
steps.risk: The instructions are the author's, so a bad page could write misleading ones. The label says whose words they are; marketplace review will need to read them.

steps.path: Pages → Weather, the first time it opens
steps.headline: The saved-key line now has a proper small button, "Use a different key", and the symbol and last line are gone.
steps.changed: The button uses the app's standard small outlined style. Pressing it changes the line to "You'll paste a different OpenWeather key next" and the main button to Continue.
steps.notice: It looks like something you can press.

steps.path: Pages → Headlines, after an edit added a second feed
steps.headline: The re-ask heading now reads "Headlines wants additional permissions".
steps.changed: Your wording replaces "wants one more thing". Symbols and the "everything else" line removed here too.
steps.notice: The heading says plainly that this is about permissions, in the app's usual word for it.

steps.path: Pages → Link reader, the first time it opens
steps.headline: The whole-internet card now spells out what that means in practice, in three short lines.
steps.changed: Under the sentence: it can load from and send to any site with no fixed list; anything you type or paste could be sent somewhere you did not choose; it still cannot see your files, your other pages, or your saved keys and sign-ins.
steps.notice: The risk and the limit are both stated, so it is neither vague nor frightening.
steps.risk: The third line stays true only while an open-internet page can never hold a key or sign-in, which you decided. If file access arrives in a later phase, that line must be revisited.

steps.path: The Task board card, opened from your phone
steps.headline: On the phone, a greyed "Finish on your computer" button sits where Allow would be, with the reason under it.
steps.changed: Under the button: "Adding a key isn't supported on the phone yet. Open this page on your computer to set it up."
steps.notice: It reads as a step you cannot take here, not as something broken.

steps.headline: The band now shows a bare "2m" and the refresh button.
steps.changed: "Updated" and "ago" are gone. It reads now, 2m, 3h, 4d.
steps.notice: The band is as quiet as it was before connections existed.
steps.risk: A bare "2m" with no label may not be understood by someone seeing it for the first time; hovering the button says "Update now".

steps.path: Pages → Trip board, after an update failed
steps.headline: The failed state follows the same short format: "Couldn't update · 3h".
steps.changed: You approved this slide as it was; I shortened "last 3 h ago" to "3h" only so the two states match. Say no to keep the longer wording here.
steps.notice: Both states of the band read the same way: a short age, then the button.

steps.path: Manage pages → a card's "2 connections" link
steps.headline: A connection not yet agreed to shows a Connect button at its bottom right, not a "waiting" label.
steps.changed: Connect closes the library and opens that page on its approval card, the one place a connection is agreed to. Approved lines keep Remove in the same spot.
steps.notice: Every line ends in one button, bottom right.
steps.risk: Connect takes you out of Manage pages rather than approving on the spot.

steps.headline: The confirm buttons are right-aligned, with Remove to the right of Never mind.
steps.notice: The button you are more likely to want first sits on the left; the destructive one is last.

steps.headline: "Connected accounts" is now "Connected services", on the Settings row and the page title.
steps.changed: The rename applies to the whole existing page, not only the new keys section, so GitHub now sits under Connected services too.
steps.notice: The name fits now that it holds keys for services as well as a GitHub sign-in.
steps.risk: Anything written elsewhere that says "Connected accounts" (help text, the docs) needs the same rename before this ships.
